To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the state spaces of the basic classes of Petni nets are characterized by the partial 2-structures of a specific kind, and that the synthesis of the state spaces of these nets can be reduced to the synthesis of partial 2-structrures of a specific kind.

(1) the state spaces of the basic classes of Petrianets can be characterized in terms of labeled partial (2)-structures and (2) the state spaces can be synthesized from the “abstract” descriptions of the nets in terms of edge-labeled graphs.

(i) the state spaces of basic subclasses of Petri nets can be characterized by means of labeled partial (in general, set) 2- structures, (ii) the state spaces can be synthesized by means of the same kind of 2-structures (with the same labels, but different partialities), and (iii) there is a close relationship between these two types of 2- structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general mathematical theory for the description and manipulation of partial (set) structures.
